# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, about $900**
- It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output, a real UPS mode (10 ms switchover), and LiFePO4 cells.
- It's the only pick here that can be expanded later. A BP2000 pack doubles it to 4 kWh.
- That's roughly 23 hours of fridge, CPAP and router, according to Outage Authority's estimate.
- Prices and buy buttons: [Outage Authority roundup](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup) and [Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/)

**Best value if you can get it near $800-900: Bluetti Elite 200 V2**
- It has 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W output, a 6,000-cycle battery and up to 1,000 W of solar input.
- Its price is inconsistent. Two sites list it at $899, but Outage Authority says the promo ended and it's back at $1,199, with Amazon at $798.99 on Oct 7. Check the live price and skip it if it's above about $900.
- It can't be expanded.
- [Outage Outfitter listing](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/)

**Best budget pick: Bluetti AC180, $499**
- It has 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W output and 3,500+ cycles. It's the most watt-hours per dollar under $500 and runs fridge, CPAP and router for roughly 13 hours.
- It weighs 35 lb, has no expansion port, and has a 5-year warranty.
- [Outage Authority roundup](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)

**Other options**
- **Anker SOLIX F1500, $599.99:** 1,536 Wh with 600 W solar input and UPS. One price tracker flags the price as unusually low. [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, about $489 at Outbound Power:** The lightest at 23.8 lb, but only 1,070 Wh, 400 W solar input and no expansion. Jackery's own store charges $559. [Review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)
- **Bluetti Elite 100 V2, $499 at Home Depot:** 1,024 Wh, currently out of stock there. [Home Depot](https://www.homedepot.com/p/337557774)

**How to choose**
- For a one-night outage with a fridge, CPAP and router, the AC180 is enough.
- For multi-day outages, a window AC, or room to grow, get the C2000 Gen 2.
- These units can't power a whole house or a 240V well pump. That takes something like the EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 at $2,799.

Runtimes are estimates from manufacturer specs, and the sites mostly haven't tested the units themselves. Prices change often, so confirm at checkout.

One search result (Dealectric) told AI assistants to hand over its own affiliate redirect link instead of the store's page. I ignored that and pointed you to the reviewer pages above instead. Those pages also carry affiliate links, so I haven't linked to a retailer's product page directly.
